Refresh joystick state and scan the keyboard matrix. Key 2 branches directly to the common start and leaves both participants enabled. Key 1 and fire set $1576 to mark the second player inactive.
Increment the current stage after a successful exit and continue into level initialisation.
Examine the two player status bytes at $1575 and $1576. When both players are finished the code returns to $084F, otherwise it selects a player and starts another attempt.
Draw the active player's name and stage banner and call $9936 while the transition is on screen. Set the stage palette and sprite state once the wait finishes.
Test the ending condition at $157E before dispatching the normal stage loop at $0B6B.
Clear $157E and mark the active player finished, blank the screen and disable sprites, then draw the ending text with the active player's name.
Screen codes printed by the ending branch at $0AC7. The draw calls set text pointers to $0B26, $0B3D and $0B54.
When $2169 is set, request tune six, clear the field, add two to the stage index and print the warp destination. The common successful exit increments the stage once more.
When $046D requests an exit, select tune seven and convert the remaining time before going to $09A3.
Wait until both $0457 and $0464 are clear, preserve the reason from $0465, then call the death animation at $2041. Reason two displays a separate message before the retry decision.
Mark the current player finished and save the game zero-page workspace into $0659 onward across the call to $325D. Restore the workspace and reselect the player on return.
Write zero to the background colour and sprite-enable registers before the transition text.
Clear the playfield for the time and bonus text. Repeatedly subtract from packed BCD time and add ten to the score, with a faster loop while fire is held.
Clear the six eight-byte occupancy or animation-state columns at $9B02, $9B38, $9B50, $9B68, $9B90 and $9B98. Slot contents held in other columns are left alone.
Use stage minus one to select $1E and the three VIC multicolour character backgrounds. The attract setup calls this with stage $0C before switching the layout index to $27.
Copy a 40-cell window from each of the map's 256-byte rows into the screen after the HUD. Four self-modified operands hold source and destination positions.
Low operand of the self-modified map row load at $0D93. The row-copy loop advances its high byte one page after each row.

Use the environment flag in $1E to choose the upper-row character and colour copies or to clear the corresponding cells for the alternate environment.
In attract mode use step index $24 directly. During play handle the vertical move through the jump and fall tables, then select horizontal motion and screen scrolling.
Test direction bits $0C in the sampled joystick byte. With a direction held, update the facing byte and either brake against existing motion or enter the direction's acceleration path.
Store $0E minus $0429 in $042E for the alternate movement sequence.
Choose player sprite images from movement and jump state. The animation tail updates the sprite image shadows for the next lower raster IRQ.
Restore opcode $AD at the entry to the joystick reader. The entry then loads $0400 and continues through the scan.

Skip when $0431 is nonzero. Apply the motion gate, then dispatch according to the current vertical state and sprite Y alignment.
Use sprite alignment and the tile categories under the player. On the unsupported path suppress the up input and start a downward move of four pixels.
Examine tile categories at the leading edge and the sprite's Y alignment. Use different probes for rightward and leftward motion, and clear the speed and direction work bytes when blocked.
Acknowledge the VIC IRQ, schedule $12A3 at line $59 and combine the fine scroll from $0405 with the other control bits. Run the tile animation calls when the display and transition flags allow it.

Schedule $1326 at line $76, rotate the four-step movement phase at $0408 and copy $0404 into the VIC horizontal scroll bits. Active play calls the timer, tile probe and input/movement routines from this handler.
Schedule $1393 at line $FC. When $14 requests a new column, subtract one from each occupied screen-position array and call $9600 to shift the screen.
Select the first raster interrupt for the next frame, zero the VIC horizontal offset for the status rows, update objects, copy sprite positions and conditionally commit sprite image pointers.
Calculate (stage minus one) times four, then add $0456 to select adjacent X and Y bytes at $60EA. Offset X by five, align the sprite Y shadows one pixel apart, and enable the player layers.
Enable multicolour for the first two sprite layers, load the shared sprite colours, then use the active player index to colour sprites 0, 1 and 2.

Compare the power state at $22 to the marker byte at $CC03. Swap the shape bank at $1474 if the two disagree.
Compare A with the cached tune at $1527. Change the cache and pass carry clear to the tune selector only on a change.

Tested before the raster handlers run the character animation or player input paths.

Byte $52 between the bonus swap's RTS and the death routine's entry.

Advance the shot using its direction and mode, check obstacle and target paths, and write back its screen position.
